packages.name: ask-espo
packages.description: Ask which skill or flow fits your situation. A router over the skills in this repo.

packages.name: code-review
packages.description: Review the changes since a fixed point (commit, branch, tag, or merge-base) along two axes — Standards (does the code follow this repo's documented coding standards?) and Spec (does the code match what the originating issue/spec asked for?). Runs both reviews in parallel sub-agents and reports them side by side. Use when the user wants to review a branch, a PR, work-in-progress changes, or asks to "review since X".

packages.name: codebase-design
packages.description: Shared vocabulary for designing deep modules. Use when the user wants to design or improve a module's interface, find deepening opportunities, decide where a seam goes, make code more testable or AI-navigable, or when another skill needs the deep-module vocabulary.

packages.name: diagnosing-bugs
packages.description: Diagnosis loop for hard bugs and performance regressions. Use when the user says "diagnose"/"debug this", or reports something broken/throwing/failing/slow.

packages.name: domain-modeling
packages.description: Build and sharpen a project's domain model. Use when the user wants to pin down domain terminology or a ubiquitous language, record an architectural decision, or when another skill needs to maintain the domain model.

packages.name: grill-me
packages.description: A relentless interview to sharpen a plan or design.

packages.name: grill-with-docs
packages.description: A relentless interview to sharpen a plan or design, which also creates docs (ADR's and glossary) as we go.

packages.name: grilling
packages.description: Grill the user relentlessly about a plan, decision, or idea. Use when the user wants to stress-test their thinking, or uses any 'grill' trigger phrases.

packages.name: handoff
packages.description: Compact the current conversation into a handoff document for another agent to pick up.

packages.name: implement
packages.description: Implement a piece of work based on a spec or set of tickets.

packages.name: improve-codebase-architecture
packages.description: Scan a codebase for deepening opportunities, present them as a visual HTML report, then grill through whichever one you pick.

packages.name: prototype
packages.description: Build a throwaway prototype to answer a design question. Use when the user wants to sanity-check whether a state model or logic feels right, or explore what a UI should look like.

packages.name: research
packages.description: Investigate a question against high-trust primary sources and capture the findings as a Markdown file in the repo. Use when the user wants a topic researched, docs or API facts gathered, or reading legwork delegated to a background agent.

packages.name: resolving-merge-conflicts
packages.description: Use when you need to resolve an in-progress git merge/rebase conflict.

packages.name: semantic-tree
packages.description: Turn a broad or tangled topic into a structured decision map that connects questions, evidence, assumptions, and next actions. Use when an idea feels larger than the first answer, several concerns are mixed together, or the user needs to see what actually changes the decision before choosing a direction.

packages.name: setup-espo-skills
packages.description: Configure this repo for the engineering skills — set up its issue tracker, triage label vocabulary, and domain doc layout. Run once before first use of the other engineering skills.

packages.name: tdd
packages.description: Test-driven development. Use when the user wants to build features or fix bugs test-first, mentions "red-green-refactor", or wants integration tests.

packages.name: teach
packages.description: Teach the user a new skill or concept, within this workspace.

packages.name: to-questionnaire
packages.description: Turn a decision you can't fully answer into a questionnaire for someone else to fill in.

packages.name: to-spec
packages.description: Turn the current conversation into a spec and publish it to the project issue tracker — no interview, just synthesis of what you've already discussed.

packages.name: to-tickets
packages.description: Break a plan, spec, or the current conversation into a set of tracer-bullet tickets, each declaring its blocking edges, published to the configured tracker — edges as text in one file per ticket locally, or native blocking links on a real tracker.

packages.name: triage
packages.description: Move issues and external PRs through a state machine of triage roles — categorise, verify, grill if needed, and write agent-ready briefs.

packages.name: wait-what
packages.description: Stop. That last message did not land — re-pitch it.

packages.name: wayfinder
packages.description: Plan a huge chunk of work — more than one agent session can hold — as a shared map of decision tickets on your issue tracker, and resolve them one at a time until the way to the destination is clear.

packages.name: wizard
packages.description: Generate an interactive bash wizard that walks a human through steps only they can perform. Use when provisioning infrastructure, setting up credentials or CI secrets, walking an unfamiliar third-party dashboard, or running a one-off migration or cutover. Don't invoke this for steps the agent can perform itself.

packages.name: writing-for-agents
packages.description: Writing documents for agents. Use when creating or editing skills, or modifying AGENTS.md or CLAUDE.md.

packages.name: youtube-action-plan
packages.description: Turn a YouTube video, transcript, or reliable summary into a small application plan with evidence, actions, and a review point. Use when a user wants to apply a video's useful ideas, separate insight from entertainment, or convert passive notes into a bounded experiment.
